canonical_claim: On GCS, non-numeric probe wrong tokens caused the dialect format guard to fail closed; LIST-derived MD5 ETags poisoned `If-Match` in GC and are disabled on generation stores; and `Expect: 100-continue` initially missed the dialect header, creating a B118-class stall risk. canonical_claim: The EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE invariant in `Build::observeAndAdmit` was guarded only by `chassert(precommitted)`, so release builds could adopt an existing incarnation without durable precommit and watermark protection. canonical_claim: The fetch-by-relink residual requires a `stageManifest` stall across at least two GC folds, every replica dropping the part ref, and a deposed leader firing `deleteExact(h,t1)` after promote. canonical_claim: Plain GET absence cannot safely authorize writer-epoch re-minting because it flattens transport or access failures into not-found; lifecycle decisions must use the authoritative probe outcome. Additionally, Same uuid plus same epoch plus an unfenced body does not prove the body came from the current writer, because a vanished epoch object can let a second same-uuid process re-mint the same pair. Additionally, If both epoch and mount control objects are wiped under a live mount, a same-pair twin can still exist briefly; the residual design relies on the surviving writer fencing on its next beat rather than allowing silently persistent dual writers.
current_evidence: src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Pool/CasServerRoot.h:274-290 documents `allocateWriterEpoch`'s absent-epoch branch: it 'uses probeSentinelRaw's authoritative outcomes, never plain get-absence (which flattens transport faults into "not found")' to decide mount absence, throwing CORRUPTED_DATA on Present/NormalMount to avoid 'a same-(uuid, epoch) twin', and requiring a TERMINAL survivor plus a fresh nonzero now_ms-derived epoch under DecommissionRecovery — exactly the residual-twin/fencing design in the claim.

canonical_claim: The ref lane can lose a durable transaction from its in-memory view and then permanently hide that transaction behind a snapshot, making the defect data-loss class.; When `tryPublishSnapshotAndAdvanceCheckpointOnce` encounters a `NeedsRecovery` lane, it recovers the durable gap before proceeding; recovery may issue its own `_ckpt` CAS, and a snapshot must never be published from the unrecovered cache. Additionally, For a `NeedsRecovery` publish attempt, recovery's checkpoint catch-up CAS must precede every snapshot-body PUT and the publisher's own checkpoint-advance CAS; the resulting published snapshot reflects the recovered frontier. Additionally, Snapshot adoption occurs only after both the snapshot body PUT and checkpoint advancement are durable; if checkpoint advancement conflicts, in-memory adoption does not occur during that failed retry unit. Additionally, After re-recovery from `NeedsRecovery`, the ref lane is `Ready`, `recoveryInstallCountForTest` has advanced, the published snapshot ID equals the durable removal transaction missing from the stale cache, and `resolveRef` for that removed ref returns absent.

canonical_claim: The B90 `ThreadGroup` fix makes a borrowed child retain a `shared_ptr` to its parent group so background work cannot use freed parent counters. Additionally, A borrowed `ThreadGroup` can outlive its parent counters when asynchronous or background work retains the query thread group after the query ends, causing use-after-free in parent counters or memory-tracking corruption. Additionally, A child `ThreadGroup` must retain a `parent_thread_group` `shared_ptr` so the parent remains alive while child trackers point to it through raw pointers.
